>> This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Dan Rodman.
White House adviser Stephen Miller begins work tomorrow as President Trump's new White
House Chief of Staff.
NPR's Winston Johnston reports he'll take the role as Democrats promise investigations
into the administration once they take control of Congress in January.
California Congressman Robert Garcia, the incoming House Oversight Chair, has warned
Trump administration officials to lawyer up.
Speaking on CNN, Attorney General Todd Blanche was asked whether representing officials investigated
by Congress is his job.
>> Every attorney general in history represents members of the administration.
And this idea that Congressman Garcia comes out and says, oh, no, no, Stephen Miller needs
his own personal lawyer, I would suggest he read the Constitution.
If he doesn't have a copy, I can arrange to send him one.
>> According to the Justice Department's website, the attorney general represents the
United States in legal matters generally and gives advice and opinions to the President
and to the heads of the executive departments of the government when requested.
Winston Johnston, NPR News, Washington.
>> Israel's president has selected center-right political leader Gotti Eisenkot to try and
form a new government in Israel.
The decision is a setback to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's efforts to stay in office
after the main political parties failed to gain a majority in the Israeli parliament.
Here's NPR's Lauren Frayer.
>> He's a former Israeli military chief.
His son was a reservist who was killed in combat in Gaza.
He's center-right as opposed to Netanyahu on the far right.
Eisenkot briefly served in Netanyahu's cabinet after the October 7th Hamas attacks.
But the two had a falling out.
Eisenkot founded a new party, ran against Netanyahu, and now wants to replace him.
Netanyahu wants to prevent that, and he is still the caretaker prime minister.
>> After meetings last week, President Isaac Herzog determined that Eisenkot has the best
chance to form a new government.
Negotiators from the US, Russia, and Ukraine will meet in Abu Dhabi Tuesday for a new round
of peace talks.
Willem Marx reports that despite objections from the Kremlin, France's European officials
also plan to be there in attendance.
Hunters Forum Minister Jean Noel Beron said Sunday his country will certainly be at the
talks alongside other European representatives.
Last week, a Kremlin spokesperson said Europe could not take part because the three-way
format had already been agreed to.
Concerns about the end goal for negotiations mediated by the US have grown since President
Trump suggested a coming deal could include "more than Ukraine," perhaps involving
parts of Europe, too.
In a CNN interview, Ukraine's President Volodymy Zelensky warned that approach could be "dangerous."
This will be the fourth round of Trump-brokered talks and the first since February.
Russia is sending a more senior delegation, but the two sides remain far apart on territorial
control and security guarantees.
For NPR News, I'm Willem Marx.
>> And you're listening to NPR News from Washington.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney is welcoming a push by congressional Democrats to repeal
some of President Trump's tariffs against Canada.
Carney has not said yet whether last Tuesday's win by Democrats in the House and Senate has
changed his trade policies.
However, he did say that lowering tariffs and restoring free trade between the two neighbors
would lower costs for both nations.
A collection of red barns, it sits inside the University of Maryland at College Park.
It's the campus farm, and it's a remnant of the university's ag school past still in
use today.
Senator Ari Daniel has more.
>> I'm a dairy cattle person.
To me, cattle are beautiful.
>> Adele Terzillo chairs the Department of Animal and Avian Sciences.
She says the students here, who largely go on to become vets, get a very hands-on education.
Liliana Sunpar is a senior.
>> I actually had the experience of helping to deliver a horse last spring.
>> This kind of learning makes her proud.
>> Yes, you can learn your chemistry, but no one can teach you how to bottle feed a
lamb unless you actually do it.
>> As a result of her studies here, Sunpar says her idea of what it means to be an impactful
vet has expanded tenfold.
For NPR News, I'm Ari Daniel.
>> Voters in Montana last Tuesday buy an almost two-to-one margin approved of ballot measure
known as Initiative 194.
It would limit corporate political spending, allowing states under the premise that if
lawmakers could not reduce political speech under Citizens United, they could stop the
spending.
I'm Dan Ronan, NPR News.
